test0.query: what is non controlling interest on balance sheet
test0.query2doc: Non-controlling interest (also called minority interest) is the portion of a subsidiary’s equity that is not owned by the parent company. On a consolidated balance sheet it appears in the equity section and represents the non-parent shareholders’ share of the subsidiary’s net assets. In consolidated financial statements the parent reports the subsidiary’s full assets, liabilities and results, but discloses the portion of net assets and net income attributable to the non-controlling owners.
